# Load gt

```{r}
malagasy <- gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/malagasy_merge_clean_no_maf_1st_degree.gt")
count_loci(malagasy)
```

This script is for the analysis of runs of homozygosity (ROH) in the Malagasy population, using the Malagasy only dataset containing `r nrow(malagasy)` individuals and `r ncol(malagasy)` loci. 

# Check Loci Order

```{r}
testthat::expect_true(is_loci_table_ordered(malagasy, error_on_false = FALSE))
```


# Find ROH

```{r}
density <- show_loci(malagasy) %>%
  group_by(chromosome, window = floor(position / 1000)) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

min_snp_coverage <- min(density$n)
median_snp_coverage <- median(density$n)
mean_snp_coverage <- mean(density$n)
```

Kirin et al 2010 plink methods: 
window of 5000 Kb
minimum number of SNPs set to 50 (particularly stringent)
1 heterozygous per window
Up to 5 missing calls per window
maximum gap between two snps set to 100 Kb
minimum length of 500 Kb (particularly stringent)
minimum density 50Kb/snp

Kourunes et al 2022 GARLIC methods:

window of 50 snps
'Using a 3-component Gaussian mixture model, GARLIC classified ROH into 3 length groups: small/class A, medium/class B, and long/class C ROH. Across all populations, class A/B and class B/C size boundaries were inferred as approximately 300kb and 1Mb, respectively'

'Since levels of ROH partitioned by size class are dependent on the size classification cutoffs, we assessed concordance of our results by repeating size classification using the –size-bounds flag in GARLIC to impose 4 additional sets of size class boundaries. We first classified ROH based on the commonly used rule of thumb that a time depth of m meioses is expected to give a mean IBD segment length of 100/m cM (Thompson 2013). In this case, common ancestors within the past 20 generations (postadmixture) would give an expected IBD segment length of approximately 2.5 Mb or longer, so we applied 2.5 Mb as the shorter/long ROH boundary. We also collected the population-specific length classification cutoffs from the 64 worldwide populations provided by Pemberton et al. (2012), which represents an extensive range of classification schemes. We repeated ROH-calling with GARLIC using the minimum, mean, and maximum of the 64 population-specific boundaries reported in Pemberton et al. (2012).'

```{r}
window_size <- 100

malagasy <- malagasy %>% group_by(population)
runs <- gt_roh_window(malagasy,
  window_size = window_size, #
  threshold = 0.05,
  min_snp = 10, # our average SNP coverage is about 1 per Kb, so this is approx 10Kb
  heterozygosity = FALSE, #
  max_opp_window = 1, #
  max_miss_window = 5, #
  max_gap = 10^5, #
  min_length_bps = 50000, #
  min_density = 0.05
) #
```

```{r}
# Load fastmixture Q matrix
qmats <- readRDS("../data/intermediate/fastmixture/fastmixture_m.RData")
mad_bor_g1000_sum <- gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean.gt")
# subset to only malagasy
all_malagasy <- c("Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "Betsileo", "Diego", "Vezo", "Mikea", "Temoro")
# tidy with the gt
tidyq <- augment(get_q_matrix(qmats, k = 3, run = 1), data = mad_bor_g1000_sum)
malagasyq <- tidyq %>% filter(population %in% all_malagasy)
# subset the malagasyq dataframe to only the "Merina"
merina <- malagasyq %>% filter(population == "Merina")
# group the merina
merina$group <- ifelse(merina$.Q3 > 0.5, "Social group A", "Social group B")
merinaA <- merina %>% filter(group == "Social group A")
merinaB <- merina %>% filter(group == "Social group B")

# match the runs$Individual and malagasy$id
matches <- match(runs$id, malagasy$id)
# add $population to runs
runs$Population <- malagasy$population[matches]
runs$Population <- as.character(malagasy$population[matches])
# if $Individual is in merinaA$id, add "merina_a" to runs$Population
runs$Population <- ifelse(runs$id %in% merinaA$id, "Merina_A", runs$Population)
# if $Individual is in merinaB$id, add "merina_b" to runs$Population
runs$Population <- ifelse(runs$id %in% merinaB$id, "Merina_B", runs$Population)
```


# Classify the runs

Use mclust 3-way Gaussian mixed-model to classify runs into 3 categories by length, similar to GALRIC method, as a test.

modelname V automatically chosen fora univariate model with variable/unequal variance

```{r}
head(runs)
classes <- mclust::Mclust(data = runs$lengthBps, G = 3) # creates the model
runs$classification <- as.factor(classes$classification)
classes$BIC # BIC values for the model, when given G = 3
```

```{r}
classes$parameters # gives details of each class
```

Now examine BIC values for 1-10 clusters, and use the clustCombiOptim function to find the optimum number of clusters.

https://rdrr.io/cran/mclust/man/clustCombi.html 

```{r}
BIC <- mclust::mclustBIC(data = runs$lengthBps, G = 1:10, modelNames = "V")
plot(BIC) # shows BIC values for G 1:10, plateaux at 3 clusters
summary(BIC)

classes_optimum <- mclust::Mclust(data = runs$lengthBps, G = 1:10, modelNames = "V") # this time G varies

clust_classes <- clustCombi(object = classes_optimum, data = runs$lengthBps) #

optimum <- clustCombiOptim(clust_classes) # returns optimum number of clusters
optimum$numClusters.combi
```


```{r}
classes <- mclust::Mclust(data = runs$lengthBps, G = optimum$numClusters.combi) # creates the model
runs$classification <- as.factor(classes$classification)
classes$BIC # BIC values for the model, when given G
classes$parameters # gives details of each class
```

We could test using Kruskal-wallis whether there is a significant diff between 
groups in both number and total length of ROH's. But, this may not answer our 
question. 

We may expect to see higher ROH's in individuals with more Asian ancestry among
the Merina, but we have several confounding effects:

1) Merina with higher African ancestry will be likely to have fewer ROH's anyway, 
as African popualtions have lower homozygosity than other global pops

2) IBD analysis (Alva et al 2022) suggests a bottleneck in the Asian ancestry 
source of all Malagasy people, meaning (if all other things were equal) the Asian 
ancestry component would have more ROH's than the African component 


Ideas:

Anything else we can use as a proxy for caste? Not really, the groups live side by 
side, so location won't help.

Correlations of ROH versus ancestry for all individuals, regardless of ethnic group
Correlations of ROH versus ethnicity for all individuals, regardless of ancestry

Analyse, see how well each explains the data

A model including the effects of both should be the best fit?


Could we remove the Merina, predict based on the correlation of ancestry/ROH's in the
other data where they should fall in ROH distribution given their ancestry, and 
then show that that model alone doesn't account for the inflation in ROH's?

```{r}
ggsave(paste0(res_dir, "mean_len_vs_asian_ancestry.jpg"), width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

Two Vezo individuals are clear outliers in the above plot. If we remove these individuals what happens?

```{r}
nrow(malagasy_all)
malagasy_all <- malagasy_all %>% filter(mean < 2000000)
nrow(malagasy_all)
```

```{r}
  )
```
